title: The Educated Barbarian: Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 5)
summary: Continuing his read of Musashi's Water Book, he relates seeing far things as near, the peripheral gaze and Musashi's grip advice to programming, lifting and grappling. He reads 'step by step walk the thousand-mile road' as the essence of natural bodybuilding and argues the only lesser men are those who gave up or preach stagnation.
claims: Musashi's advice to see distant things as close and close things from a distance means big things are made of small details; you need to zoom in and out
Musashi's peripheral gaze, seeing to the sides without moving head or eyes, saves time in combat because turning the head is slow
He practised always looking straight ahead using only peripheral vision; it is mentally taxing and looks odd, but people make way for you because they assume you are going straight
Applied to programming, the gaze means keeping your goal in sight and building everything around it; focusing on one section at a time leaves puzzle pieces that do not fit
The trade-off of peripheral perception is that you lose fine detail on what you are not focused on
Real gripping is done by the last three fingers, which is where lifters get calluses; his judo instructor threw students around using only three fingers
With a barbell you need all fingers because the bar is thick; any play in the hand roughly halves grip strength, so set the fingers before pulling so the bar cannot shift
Take a weight you can deadlift double overhand, give the bar some play in your hands and pull: it will not come up because the bar pries the hand open
Being excellent at something does not make you good at explaining it, yet explaining is how knowledge circulates and a community improves
Concepts you learn are worthless unless you turn them into actions
Natural bodybuilding is walking a thousand-mile road step by step; trying to make huge headway each session, like training twice a week and killing yourself, leads to injury and no progress
Lifting means studying strategy for years, technique and programming; you are never done, which is the beauty of it
Do not compare yourself to others; it leads either to depression or to ego, so aim only to beat yourself of yesterday
The lesser men are those who gave up; a 10-year lifter who is stagnant and preaches limits is less of a warrior than a 2-year lifter still progressing
Victory over lesser men also means leading and inspiring those who have given up rather than getting upset at them
